issues.failure_explanation: For a scalar row A=(1), b=1 and x=0, the displayed update gives x_1=-1, while the orthogonal projection onto A x=b gives x_1=1. The same sign error appears in the block update, which should add B^\dagger(b_B-Bx_k), not B^\dagger(Bx_k-b_B).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the signs in the recalled scalar and block updates to x_k + (b_i-<A_i,x_k>)A_i/||A_i||^2 and x_k + B^\dagger(b_B-Bx_k).
issues.overall_effect: The recalled baseline Kaczmarz and block-Kaczmarz projection formulas are false. The proposed regularized ROR-BK update later uses the correct sign, so the main algorithm is not directly altered.
issues.title: Sign error in recalled Kaczmarz and block-Kaczmarz projection updates
issues.why_classification: A one-line sign correction restores the standard projection formulas and loses no substantive claim of the proposed method.

&=I-\tilde{\lambda}(A_\tau^TA_\tau+\tilde{\lambda}I)^{-1}\label{eq:errbound2}

issues.failure_explanation: The regularized update error matrix is λ(A_τ^TA_τ+λI)^{-1}, which has eigenvalue 1 on null(A_τ). The claimed factor λ/(λ_min^+(A_τ^TA_τ)+λ) is therefore not a uniform norm bound unless the error has no component in null(A_τ); the theorem does not assume x_0∈R(A_τ^T) or the needed full-range condition. Example: A=[1 0;0 1], two row blocks, b=0, x_0=e_2, λ=1; selecting block [1 0] leaves the error norm 1, violating the stated factor 1/2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish a valid contraction on the invariant subspace, e.g. use squared-error expectations, assume the union of sampled block ranges spans R(A^T) and the initial error lies there, and derive a correct rate.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised exponential mean-error convergence bound for ROR-BK is false or unsupported; any guarantee based on it is unreliable.
issues.title: Regularized ROR-BK error bound is false for nullspace components
issues.why_classification: A central convergence guarantee fails as stated, and no comparable rate follows from the source without new analysis or major weakening.

issues.failure_explanation: The derived bounds contain ratios ||A_S e||^2/λ_max(S) and ||A_S e||^2/λ_min(S). Maximizing only the numerator over candidate row sets S does not maximize these ratios when the eigenvalues depend on S. For example, S1 may have larger residual but much larger λ_max than S2, giving a smaller reduction in the upper bound.
